name: Slant 6
label: Dischord
lede: Christina Billotte left Autoclave for something faster, took a 1963 Silvertone and a drummer who learned the instrument to join, and made two albums in three years. The New York Times later called one of them arguably the best album of the riot grrrl era.

eras.title: A slant six and a Silvertone
eras.text: After Autoclave, Christina Billotte wanted something simpler and faster. She found it in bassist Myra Power and Marge Marshall, an English trumpet player who agreed to learn the drums, and in a scene of house parties and fashion shows shared with Nation of Ulysses.

q: Something more straightforward than Autoclave, more danceable.
years.h: Billotte starts over after Autoclave, with a drummer who's new to drums
years.p: [[Christina Billotte|62325e5d-014f-42a1-90d5-fa12e17aa214]] takes guitar and vocals and [[Myra Power|90cf6dcb-e8f5-4b69-be33-3e365b6be4ae]] plays bass. Marge Marshall, an English trumpet and piano player, gets talked into the drums, per Bandcamp Daily.
years.xp:
The name comes from Chrysler's slant-six engine, which Bandcamp Daily reads as a nod to the golden age of American carmaking. Billotte played a 1963 Silvertone, made around the same time as the engine, through the whole run. Bandcamp Daily hears post-punk austerity, surf twang and Link Wray rumble in it.

Wikipedia dates the start to July 1992 in Washington. Billotte has said she wanted major-key songs and more energy this time, a turn away from Autoclave's knots.

years.h: Famous Monsters house parties, with Nation of Ulysses
years.p: Dischord says Slant 6 worked with members of [[Nation of Ulysses|ae888df0-2a19-4895-a654-e0093875d5b6]] on recordings, fashion shows and a run of performance house parties called Famous Monsters.

years.h: The first single, What Kind of Monster Are You?, is Dischord No. 85
years.p: Slant 6's debut 7" lands on Dischord. Wikipedia dates it 1993, Bandcamp Daily early 1994. Here's the band at Fort Reno Park in Washington on July 23, 1993.

eras.title: Soda Pop * Rip Off
eras.text: Slant 6's debut album fit thirteen songs into 34 minutes and put hooks where nobody expected them. The Chicago Reader compared the band to early Wire: say the bit and move on.

years.h: Soda Pop * Rip Off arrives as Dischord No. 91
years.p: Thirteen songs in 34 minutes, produced by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]]. Rolling Stone singled out the groove of Time Expired.
years.xp:
Bandcamp Daily hears the Wipers, Wire, the Gories and the Breeders in it. The Chicago Reader went with early Wire.

Here's the band playing What Kind of Monster Are You? at the Fireside Bowl in Chicago on December 10, 1994, per the uploader.

years.h: Slant 6 turn up in the indie road movie Half-Cocked
years.p: Wikipedia lists Slant 6 in the 1994 film and credits them with a track on its soundtrack.

eras.title: Stranger, darker, then England
eras.text: Inzombia came out stranger and darker. Then came the band's only trip to England, supporting Fugazi in rooms far bigger than any D.C. house party, and Slant 6 broke up before the tour ended.

years.p: Recorded at Inner Ear and produced by the band and Ian MacKaye. Twelve songs, from G.F.S. to the title track, with Retro Duck and Eight Swimming Pools in between.

years.h: A split single with The Make-Up puts two Famous Monsters bands on one record
years.p: Slant 6 share a Time Bomb Records single with [[The Make-Up|26cad87d-5be0-467f-955f-b3ccecce007a]], the band Ian Svenonius and James Canty formed after Nation of Ulysses, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Slant 6 open for Fugazi at the Manchester Academy
years.p: The Fugazi Live Series logs Slant 6 and Fabric supporting [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] on May 7, 1995, the night after Brighton, in front of 1,200 people.

years.h: Last show in Leeds, then Slant 6 are done
years.p: Dischord says the band broke up on the 1995 English tour with Fugazi, after a final show in Leeds. Christina Billotte goes on to [[Quix*o*tic|e4ad9a5b-7358-46be-9d34-73e9b9d072ec]] and [[The Casual Dots|d74e8159-d217-4a24-8ef0-5c2aab85a308]].

eras.title: Arguably the best
eras.text: No reunion, just the records, and a slow critical climb until the big papers caught up with what D.C. had been saying all along.

years.h: Washington City Paper reviews the Soda Pop * Rip Off reissue
years.p: The review says Billotte was a better singer than many of her '90s contemporaries.

years.big: One of my all-time favourite groups.
years.h: The New York Times calls Soda Pop * Rip Off arguably the best of the riot grrrl era
years.p: Mary Timony, Billotte's Autoclave bandmate, on Slant 6.
years.xp: Rolling Stone's Rob Sheffield has called the album an essential LP of the nineties, and Pitchfork an enduring model of punk rock poise.
